problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:

* Container 1: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue 116 credits
* Container 2: volume 41 cubic meters, revenue 162 credits
* Container 3: volume 5 cubic meters, revenue 119 credits
* Container 4: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue 53 credits
* Container 5: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue 91 credits
* Container 6: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue 232 credits
* Container 7: volume 41 cubic meters, revenue 176 credits
* Container 8: volume 19 cubic meters, revenue 90 credits
* Container 9: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue 276 credits
* Container 10: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue 13 credits
* Container 11: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue 77 credits
* Container 12: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue 43 credits
* Container 13: volume 1 cubic meter, revenue 167 credits
* Container 14: volume 29 cubic meters, revenue 147 credits
* Container 15: volume 13 cubic meters, revenue 273 credits
* Container 16: volume 35 cubic meters, revenue 81 credits
* Container 17: volume 41 cubic meters, revenue 184 credits
* Container 18: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue 79 credits
* Container 19: volume 12 cubic meters, revenue 175 credits
* Container 20: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue 161 credits
* Container 21: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue 240 credits
* Container 22: volume 31 cubic meters, revenue 222 credits
* Container 23: volume 12 cubic meters, revenue 242 credits
* Container 24: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue 145 credits
* Container 25: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue 224 credits
* Container 26: volume 42 cubic meters, revenue 233 credits

The vessel has a maximum capacity of 444 cubic meters. Choose the container combination that yields the highest total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
